full_judgment: 4. Let me now proceed to apply the principle laid down by the Appellate Division to the facts and circumstances of the present case. In this case the defendant petitioner examined 2 witnesses on his side. D.W. 1 is Fazal Ahmed, the defendant No. 2 himself. He has not uttered a single word to say that the document was read over to the plaintiff (the lady) and that she executed it after understanding the transaction. D.W. 2 Mvi Ahmadul Hoq is the deed writer. He had said that the plaintiff had put her thumb impression in his presence. He has further stated that after the document was read over to her she admitted that she had received consideration. There is also nothing in his evidence to show that the plaintiff had understood the nature and purport of the transaction. Ext. A is the certified copy of the deed of gift. Exits B and B (1) are certified copies of the Sale-deeds. It appears that Ahmadul Hoq was the scribe of all the three documents. Abdul Khaleque, Jabar Mulluk and Kala Meah are the common attested witnesses But none of the attesting witnesses has been examined and no explanation has forth come as to why they have not been examined. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, non examination of these attesting witnesses cannot but he viewed with serious suspicion and the evidence of the defendant No. 2, who is a recipient in all the three deeds and that of the deed writer alone can by no means be considered to be either suitable or satisfactory. From the above discussions it is evident that the defendant petitioner who seeks to bind the plaintiff-opposite party, the transferor who is a purdanashin illiterate lady, to the terms of the disputed documents has failed to discharge onus that lay and always lay on him and to satisfy the Court that she substantially understood the transaction and executed the deeds with full understanding of what she was doing and of the nature of the transaction. This by itself and without any further enquiry was sufficient to reject the claim of the defendant-petitioner based on the disputed documents. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I would, however, also hold the defendant petitioner was also required to prove that the plaintiff purdanashin illiterate lady had independent advice. In the instant case, at the relevant time the plaintiff was living jointly with the defendant No. 2 petitioner and the defendant No. 1 respondent, who were her sons and they were looking after her during her illness. She was an octogenarian Indy. it i.e evidence the defendant No. 2, the done in Ext. A and the defendants Nos. 1 and 2, the joint recipients in Exts. B, and B (1) stood in a position of active confidence and in dependent advice was also an essential burden to be discharged which was not done. The plaintiff title to the suit-lands was admitted. The learned Subordinate Judge has found that the plaintiff is also in possession. This finding about possession could not be and has not been assailed before me. The plaintiff was entitled to a decree and the learned Subordinate Judge has rightly decreed the suit in reversal of the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif. The learned Subordinate Judge has not committed any error of law in his decision and no interference by this Court is called for.
